items.title:
THE LONGEVITY PROMISE

Are anti-ageing drugs finally here—or are we getting ahead of the science?

A recent BBC Science Focus article suggests medications capable of slowing biological ageing may already be available.

It’s an intriguing proposition. And unlike much of the commercial longevity industry, the underlying science deserves to be taken seriously.

But there’s an important distinction between drugs that influence ageing-related biological pathways and drugs that demonstrably extend healthy human life.

I’ve reviewed the article alongside the clinical evidence, including recent randomized trials of metformin, rapamycin and senolytic therapies.

The findings are genuinely interesting. Some are encouraging. Others are considerably less impressive than the headlines suggest.

Let’s separate what we know, what we suspect, and what remains to be demonstrated.

A thread. 🧵
